logline: Ryan Murphy's true-crime anthology reconstructs defining American legal and political scandals - the O.J. Simpson trial, the Gianni Versace murder, the Clinton-Lewinsky affair - through the perspectives of people the official record flattened into symbols.

renewal.note: Three-season anthology concluded November 9, 2021 on FX. A fourth season tentatively titled Studio 54 was announced but has seen no production progress as of mid-2024.

bollymeter.basis: 97% on Rotten Tomatoes across 93 reviews; The People v. O.J. Simpson was considered the definitive re-examination of the 1995 trial - NPR and Daily Mail praised the performances and the direction as extraordinary at every level.

pull_quotes.text: The performances here are amazing. Cuba Gooding Jr. is a ball of angry narcissism, and Sarah Paulson brings wounded humanity.
The writing is sharp. It is blissfully directed, without a single wasted scene.

seasons.review_body: The People v. O.J. Simpson earned 97% on Rotten Tomatoes across 93 reviews and became one of the most decorated television series of 2016, winning multiple Emmy, Golden Globe, and SAG Awards including Outstanding Limited Series. The critical consensus held that the season accomplished something the trial-as-spectacle had made nearly impossible: restoring human specificity to figures who had become archetypes. Sarah Paulson's Marcia Clark was widely cited as the season's revelatory performance - a depiction of a woman systematically destroyed by the same media apparatus that was nominally reporting on justice. Cuba Gooding Jr.'s O.J. was praised as precisely calibrated narcissism. NPR's Eric Deggans called the performances amazing; the Daily Mail called the direction blissful. The season's interrogation of race, celebrity, and legal process in America was considered prestige television at its most socially useful.

episode_reviews.title: From the Ashes of Tragedy
episode_reviews.review_body: 'From the Ashes of Tragedy' announces the structural intelligence that makes 'The People v. O.J. Simpson' a landmark television achievement. The audience knows the verdict, knows OJ Simpson's name, knows the Bronco chase from the original news coverage. Creator Scott Alexander and Larry Karaszewski, working from Jeffrey Toobin's book, use this prior knowledge not as a handicap but as a structural resource: since the question is not what happened but why it happened that way, the premiere can immediately begin investigating the institutional failures, racial contexts, and media dynamics that turned a double murder trial into the defining American media event of the 1990s. The Bronco chase is framed from inside the LA newsroom - the machine processing an event in real time - rather than from the public street. The ensemble (Cuba Gooding Jr., Sarah Paulson, Courtney B. Vance, Sterling K. Brown, David Schwimmer) is given enough scene time in the premiere to establish nine separate characters without crowding. 99% RT on the season.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the season's structural approach - not whodunit (the audience already knows) but how: how did the most watched criminal trial in American history become a referendum on race, police credibility, and celebrity before it became about two murders? The episode frames the Bronco chase from inside the media machine rather than the public street.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The news broadcast of the Bronco chase, reframed as institutional failure rather than spectacle - the moment the season announces it will not be what audiences expect.

episode_reviews.title: The Verdict
episode_reviews.review_body: 'The Verdict' is the season's formal climax, and Ryan Murphy deploys the show's accumulated argument in a single, almost wordless sequence: the verdict reading, and the reaction shots that follow. The audience in the courtroom - and by extension, the audience watching - is divided by race and by prior expectation in ways the show has spent nine episodes carefully charting. The not guilty verdict's emotional register depends entirely on who is in the frame and what they brought with them. The show does not editorialize; it simply holds the camera on faces that contain the entire history of what the trial was actually about. Courtney B. Vance's Johnnie Cochran and Sarah Paulson's Marcia Clark anchor the finale with performances that have already established their characters' histories so thoroughly that no additional scene is needed. 99% RT. One of the three or four best American limited series ever made.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale covers the verdict and its immediate aftermath. The show's formal achievement here is treating a moment the audience already knows as genuinely suspenseful by shifting the focus from the outcome to the reactions - a roomful of people split by race and prior expectation, each face its own history of America.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The reaction shots during the not guilty verdict - the season's entire argument delivered without a single word of dialogue.

Darren Criss channels Tom Ripley as Andrew Cunanan - the most confident person in the room and the most insecure.

seasons.review_body: The Assassination of Gianni Versace earned 88% on Rotten Tomatoes across 97 reviews and delivered Darren Criss's career-defining performance as Andrew Cunanan - a study in the specific damage done by a particular American psychology: the driven, beautiful, systematically ignored. The season's reverse chronology structure (beginning with Versace's murder and moving backward through Cunanan's killing spree) was cited as the season's formal intelligence: by the time the audience understood Cunanan's origin, the show had already made them complicit in his glamour. The RT consensus called it a career-defining performance anchoring an intricate murder mystery. Decider named it one of the best dramas of the decade. The season deepened the anthology's project - not just reconstructing events but examining the cultural conditions that made them possible.
seasons.season_over_season: A distinct creative mode from Season 1 - the reverse chronology is a formal bet that pays off, and the focus on the perpetrator rather than the legal system gives the anthology a new dimension.

bollymeter.basis: 69% on Rotten Tomatoes across 74 reviews; Beanie Feldstein and Sarah Paulson's performances were praised but critics found the season unable to decide between humanising its subjects and indulging the media circus it claimed to critique.

pull_quotes.text: Determined, detailed, and ultimately humane, Impeachment: American Crime Story thoroughly rewrites the book on the Clinton-Lewinsky scandal.

seasons.review_body: Impeachment earned 69% on Rotten Tomatoes across 74 reviews - the lowest critical standing of the anthology's three seasons. The RT consensus identified the season's central creative tension: it could not decide whether it was unearthing the humanity of a presidential scandal or indulging the mythology of its media circus. Monica Lewinsky herself was a producer, and Beanie Feldstein's performance was universally praised as a genuine act of historical rehabilitation. Sarah Paulson as Linda Tripp was described as transformative. The critical division fell on the show's structural handling of political culpability - whether the season adequately contextualised Bill Clinton's role while centering the women who were destroyed by the scandal's aftermath. The Age called it a consolation prize at best; Film School Rejects found it ultimately humane and thoroughgoing.
seasons.season_over_season: The anthology's weakest creative season - the subject matter demanded a clarity of moral perspective that the show's structural ambivalence could not provide.
